ideas.evidence_quote: with the right size, convolutional tokenization, transformers can avoid overfitting and outperform state-of-the-art CNNs on small datasets
ideas.hypothesis: A compact transformer using convolutional tokenization (rather than fixed-size patch embedding) can be adapted to the 28x28x3 PathMNIST input, leveraging the fact that CCT demonstrated competitive accuracy on CIFAR-10 (32x32x3) with only 3.7M parameters. For PathMNIST's ~90K training samples across 9 classes, a similarly sized conv-tokenized transformer (1-4M params) with 2-4 attention layers may avoid overfitting while capturing inter-pixel dependencies that a plain CNN misses, particularly for subtle histological patterns.

ideas.evidence_quote: a pure transformer applied directly to sequences of image patches can perform very well on image classification tasks
ideas.hypothesis: Applying a pure self-attention mechanism over a small number of spatial tokens (e.g., 4 tokens from 14x14 patches or 16 tokens from 7x7 patches) on the 28x28x3 PathMNIST input could model global tissue-context relationships (e.g., gland architecture, stromal patterns) that local convolutions struggle to capture, provided the token count is kept small to avoid overfitting on ~90K samples.

ideas.evidence_quote: All images are pre-processed into a small size of 28x28 (2D) or 28x28x28 (3D) with the corresponding classification labels so that no background knowledge is required for users.
ideas.hypothesis: Because PathMNIST images are standardized to 28x28 with no required domain preprocessing, the architecture should be lightweight (fewer than 5M parameters) to match the dataset's design intent for 'lightweight 2D images' and to prevent overfitting given the moderate class sizes (7.8K-12.9K per class). A shallow CNN backbone (3-5 conv blocks) with global average pooling is a strong baseline to beat.

ideas.evidence_quote: GhostNet-VGG is shown to be the most robust to overall performance drop at lower precision.
ideas.hypothesis: GhostNet-VGG-style architecture (combining ghost modules for cheap feature generation with VGG-like depth) is a robust backbone for PathMNIST, as it was shown to be the most robust to performance degradation under quantization. Even without quantization, its efficient feature generation may provide a favorable bias-variance trade-off for the 28x28x3 pathology input with 9 classes.

ideas.evidence_quote: We find that temperature scaling can improve calibration error for quantized networks, with some caveats.
ideas.hypothesis: Applying temperature scaling as a post-hoc calibration step during training on PathMNIST can improve the reliability of predicted class probabilities, which is important for medical decision support. This is a low-cost training modification that does not change the architecture and can be validated on the training split.

ideas.evidence_quote: Our findings highlight the trade-offs between computational speed and model accuracy, offering valuable insights for researchers and practitioners in medical image analysis.
ideas.hypothesis: The choice of deep-learning framework (Keras vs PyTorch vs JAX) introduces measurable differences in training efficiency and convergence behavior on PathMNIST. Selecting the framework with the best accuracy-per-second trade-off for a 28x28x3, 9-class problem can reduce wall-clock training time without sacrificing final accuracy, which is relevant for iterative experimentation.

ideas.evidence_quote: We also analyse the impact of data augmentation on the quality of unlearning.
ideas.hypothesis: Data augmentation (particularly horizontal flipping) serves as a critical regularizer for PathMNIST training, as evidenced by its measured impact on model quality in related medical image classification experiments. Given the moderate per-class sample sizes (7.8K-12.9K), augmentation can effectively double the training signal and reduce overfitting risk.

proposals.description: Apply horizontal flip (hflip) as the sole geometric augmentation during PathMNIST training. Pathology tissue sections do not have a strict left-right asymmetry that would change the histological class (e.g., cell morphology, gland architecture, stromal pattern remain invariant under left-right mirroring). Vertical flip, 90-degree, and 180-degree rotations are excluded because tissue orientation (e.g., direction of collagen fibers, apical-basal polarity of epithelial cells, orientation of glandular structures) can be diagnostically meaningful and flipping/rotating may alter the visual signature of certain classes. This conservative augmentation strategy preserves label semantics while providing a 2x effective training set.
proposals.label_preservation_rationale: Horizontal mirroring preserves the morphological features that define pathology classes (cell shape, nuclear-to-cytoplasmic ratio, gland architecture, stromal density) because these features are not directionally encoded in the left-right axis. In contrast, vertical or rotational transforms could invert apical-basal polarity or alter the perceived orientation of tissue structures, potentially changing the visual appearance of class-specific patterns.

proposals.description: A non-executable architecture specification for a compact transformer adapted to 28x28x3 PathMNIST input. (1) Convolutional tokenizer: a 3x3 conv (stride 2, 32 filters) followed by a 3x3 conv (stride 2, 64 filters) producing a 7x7x64 feature map, then reshaped to 49 tokens of dimension 64. (2) Positional encoding: learnable 49x64 positional embeddings added to tokens. (3) Transformer encoder: 3 layers, each with multi-head self-attention (4 heads, head_dim=16), layer norm, and a 2x64 FFN with GELU activation. (4) Classification head: global average pooling over the 49 tokens, a linear layer (64 to 128), ReLU, dropout (0.3), and a final linear layer (128 to 9) for the 9 PathMNIST classes. Total parameter budget approximately 1.5-2.5M. This design follows the CCT principle of convolutional tokenization to avoid the data-hungry nature of fixed patch embeddings while retaining self-attention for global context modeling on the small 28x28 input.
implementation_requirements: Input tensor shape must be (batch, 28, 28, 3) with 3-channel RGB pathology images
Convolutional tokenizer must produce exactly 49 tokens of dimension 64 via two stride-2 convolutions
Learnable positional embeddings of shape (49, 64) must be added before the first attention layer
Each transformer layer must use pre-norm (LayerNorm before attention and FFN) with 4 attention heads of dimension 16
FFN intermediate dimension must be 2x the embedding dimension (128) with GELU activation
Classification head must use global average pooling over token dimension, then a single hidden linear layer with dropout 0.3
Total trainable parameters must not exceed 3M to maintain data efficiency on ~90K training samples
Output must be a (batch, 9) logit vector for the 9 PathMNIST classes
Training should use cross-entropy loss with class-weighted sampling to address the mild imbalance (7886-12885 per class)
Horizontal flip augmentation should be applied during training as the sole geometric transform
